senses.gloss: (v. precd.; cmp. רִיחַ) to evaporate, be decomposed; to decay; to smell badly.—Part. pass. סָרוּחַ; f. סְרוּחָה; pl. סְרוּחִים, סְרוּחִין; סְרוּחוֹת.

units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 71b:19">Snh. 71ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Ketubot 45a:1">Keth. 45ᵃ</cite> <he>סָרְחָה ולבסוף בגרה</he> if she sinned (had intercourse) and afterwards became of age.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 13">Num. R. s. 13</cite> <he>אם אינה סוֹרַחַת … ואם סורחת מלקה</he> (not <he>סוחרת</he>) is she (the ass whom he rides) is not mischievous, he does not strike her, but if she is, he strikes her; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 554">Yalk. Lev. 554</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 959:16">Yalk. Prov. 959</cite>.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 959:16">Ib.</cite> <he>שאם יִסְרַח יהא וכ׳</he> to chastise him with them in case he should offend.

<cite ref="Yoma 75a:15">Yoma 75ᵃ</cite> <he>הוא ס׳ עלי</he> he (my husband) acted offensively towards me; <he>היא סרחה וכ׳</he> she acted offensively &c. Ib. 77ᵃ <he>סרחה אומתך</he> thy people has degenerated.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 6:2">Midr. Till. to Ps. VI</cite> <he>סרחה עליו מדינתו</he> one of his provinces rebelled against him.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 43:8">Ex. R. s. 43</cite> <he>סָרַחְתָּ כל הסרחון הזה וכ׳</he> thou hast done all that mischief, and thou criest? <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 42:8">Ex. R. s. 42</cite> <he>לא היה לכם לִסְרוֹחַ וכ׳</he> you ought not to have sinned either on the second or the third day, but must you sin on the very first day?; a. fr.—
senses.label: a

units: Sot. IX, 15 (49ᵇ) והכמות סופרים תִּסְרַח (or תִּסָּרֵחַ Nif.) and the wisdom of the scholars shall become vapid (v.
<cite ref="Jeremiah 49:7">Jer. XLIX, 7</cite>); <cite ref="Sanhedrin 97a">Snh. 97ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:13">Cant. R. to II, 13</cite>; Yalk. Am. 549.—Part. pass. as ab.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:8">Cant. R. to IV, 8</cite> <he>דיעה ס׳ וכ׳</he> that senseless fool &c., v. <cite ref="D00943"><he>דֵּעָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20">Num. R. s. 20</cite>; Tanḥ. Bal. 9 (ref. to the peculiar expression in<cite ref="Numbers 22:29">Num. XXII, 29</cite>) <he>אע״פ … לשונו ס׳</he> even when speaking the sacred tongue, the gentile’s speech is tasteless (or obscene).
senses.label: b

units: <cite ref="Chagigah 5b:5">Ḥag. 5ᵇ</cite> (ref. to Jer. l. c.) <he>כיון שאבדה … נִסְרַחַת וכ׳</he> when counsel was gone from the children (of Israel), the wisdom of the nations became vapid.

<cite ref="Shabbat 62b:12">Sabb. 62ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <he>סרחים</he>, <cite ref="Amos 6:4">Am. VI, 4</cite>) <he>מַסְרִיחִין וכ׳</he> make their beds offensive with effusion &c.; <cite ref="Kiddushin 71b">Kidd. 71ᵇ</cite>. Tanḥ. Vaëra 14 <he>הִסְרִיחוּ מצרים</he> they made Egypt stink; a. e.

senses.gloss: to become vapid, putrid; to smell badly.
units: <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:13">Cant. R. to II, 13</cite> <he>היין יַסְרִיחַ</he> the wine will become vapid (Sot. l. c., a. e. <he>היין ביוקר</he>).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 34:10">Gen. R. s. 34</cite> <he>הוא מַסְרִיחַ</he> it becomes putrid; <he>ואינה מַסְרַחַת</he> without decaying. Tanḥ. l. c. <he>ויַסְרִיחוּ במצרים</he> and spread stench in Egypt.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 391:14">Yalk. Ex. 391</cite> <he>חלבנה … מסרחת</he> galbanum gives only an offensive smell; a. fr.
